passages.heard: Napoleon sits down to play chess against a machine.  Legend says he cheats on purpose  and the machine sweeps every piece right off the board.
This is the Turk, a mechanical man in a turban sitting on a big wooden cabinet full of gears.  It was built in 1770 and for more than 80 years it amazed people across Europe and America.

people said it had to be a trick.  So before a game, the showman opened every door  and shone a candle right through the machinery.  Nothing in there but gears.  Then he'd wind it up, the head would turn,  and it would play, and it usually won.

You see, it was like a magic box with a false bottom. Hidden inside was a real chess master,  on a sliding seat. As each door opened, he slid out of sight.  Magnets under the board showed him every move, and levers worked the arm.

In 1854, the Turk burned in a museum fire.  A few years later, the owner's son finally revealed the secret, and today, Amazon runs  a service where hidden humans do the work computers can't.  Its name?  Mechanical Turk.
